body: James Warne and his son Ted cycled from Noss Mayo, near Plymouth, to Fair Havens adults' hospice in Southend, arriving on Saturday 31 October after six days on the road. They rode in memory of Ted's grandfather, Paul Wellsteed, who was cared for at Fair Havens before he died in June.
The pair covered about 80km a day through rain and mist, and took a day off to rest when both fell ill. The family moved to Devon from Leigh-on-Sea eight years ago.

community.headline: Chelmsford parents back Havens Hospices appeal after baby son's care
community.summary: Michael and Sarah Fragnito's son Elio spent his last two days at the Little Havens children's hospice. They now support its Christmas appeal.
body: Elio Fragnito became critically unwell within 36 hours of his birth. Doctors at Great Ormond Street Hospital found a rare and serious heart condition that had not been picked up during pregnancy. When the family were told nothing more could be done, they chose Little Havens, the children's hospice in Thundersley run by Havens Hospices. Elio died there aged 36 days.

His parents told Havens Hospices that staff helped them bathe him for the first time, arranged family photographs and let them take him outside to feel the rain. "Grief is awful, but love comes out on top," they said.
The Chelmsford couple are backing the charity's Big Yes! Christmas Appeal, which asks the community to help fund the care its nurses give.
points: Elio was born with a rare heart condition

courts.headline: Brentwood man charged with rape at Soho's Groucho Club
courts.summary: Stefan-Pierre Tomlin, 36, is due at Southwark Crown Court on Monday. He also faces two counts of assault by penetration.
body: A Brentwood man has been charged with rape over an alleged incident at the Groucho Club, the private members' club in Soho, central London, two years ago.

Stefan-Pierre Tomlin, 36, faces one count of rape and two counts of assault by penetration. The Crown Prosecution Service authorised the charges in September, after a Metropolitan Police investigation.
He first appeared at Southend Magistrates' Court on Monday 2 November and was granted bail. He is next due at Southwark Crown Court on Monday 30 November.

The Met began investigating after a woman reported that she had been raped inside the club, in Dean Street, on Wednesday 13 November 2024. Specialist officers supported her, and at the time the force said there was no suggestion that any of the club's staff were involved.

Westminster City Council suspended the club's licence later that month at the request of police. The club, long a haunt of writers, artists and stars of film and television, reopened in January 2025 under new conditions.
Mr Tomlin, a model, was widely reported in 2017 to be Tinder's most popular user.
By law, the woman is entitled to lifelong anonymity.
points: Alleged incident: 13 November 2024

courts.headline: Essex steel firm fined £12,000 over false papers for Chelmsford gas platform
courts.summary: An Essex steel company supplied false safety paperwork for a platform holding up a Chelmsford gas main. It has been fined and must pay costs.
body: J.T.L. Steel Fabrications (U.K.) Ltd has been fined £12,000 at City of London Magistrates' Court, the government's Office for Product Safety and Standards (OPSS) announced on Wednesday 25 November.

The company made a structural steel platform that supports a stepped-down high-pressure gas main and plant in Chelmsford. According to Construction Enquirer and UKPulse, it supplied the platform with falsified documents: a factory production control certificate, a declaration of performance and a declaration of conformity. That broke the Construction Products Regulations 2013, which require makers to prove structural products meet safety standards.

On top of the fine, the firm was ordered to pay £12,048 in costs and a £2,000 victim surcharge. Baroness Blake, the minister for building safety, said there "can be no shortcuts" on building safety. Neither report gives the date of the hearing or where in Essex the company is based.

courts.headline: Harwich firm and University of Essex test VR for helicopter rescue crews
courts.summary: Psychologists worked with Air Rescue UK, which trains helicopter winch crews in Harwich, on a simulator that lets them practise emergencies too dangerous to stage for real.

also.name: University of Essex: the full report
Air Med & Rescue: Air Rescue UK's Harwich centre

body: Virtual reality could help helicopter rescue crews practise emergencies that are too dangerous to stage in the air, research by the University of Essex and Air Rescue UK suggests. Air Rescue UK trains helicopter winch crews at its centre in Harwich.

Psychologists from the university looked at how virtual and mixed reality could add to the training of helicopter hoist operators. These crew members run the winch during a rescue, guiding the pilot while keeping watch on the weather, obstacles, the aircraft and the person being lifted.
Training on real flights is expensive and carries risks. Some situations, such as severe weather, equipment failures and dangerous seas, cannot safely be set up on purpose, the university said.
## A simulator with a real cable

The team assessed Air Rescue UK's mixed-reality simulator and reviewed earlier research. The system pairs a virtual scene with real equipment, including a hoist cable that recreates the pull and movement operators feel on a real mission.

Trainees can practise a runaway winch, a fouled cable, an engine failure and an emergency cut of the hoist cable, as well as rough conditions. Up to 92% of evaluations after training showed trainees felt they had learned something new or sharpened their skills.

The researchers also found that the harder a session felt mentally, the more operators felt they had learned. They say training could one day be matched to experience, easing beginners in and giving old hands tougher, time-pressured emergencies.
## What they said
Dr Claire Oakley, a research associate on the project, said: "What is exciting about virtual reality is that it allows us to study decision-making under pressure in a safe and controlled way."
Understanding those processes better could help the team design more effective training for rescue crews, she added.

A spokesperson for Air Rescue UK said the company was "pleased with the early results" of the partnership. It said the work had laid the groundwork for hoist training that meets the needs of new and experienced operators, helicopter operators, the industry and the regulator.
## Trained in Harwich

Air Rescue UK opened its training centre at Sentinel House in Harwich in 2025, its 10th anniversary year, [Air Med & Rescue magazine reported](https://www.airmedandrescue.com/latest/news/new-training-center-air-rescue-uk). The Lord-Lieutenant of Essex, Jennifer Tolhurst, opened the building.

The project was backed by the University of Essex Innovation Fund and led by Professor Miroslav Sirota, with Dr Oakley and Professor Marie Juanchich. Dr Motonori Yamaguchi, now at Shimane University in Japan, and Ian Bonthrone of Air Rescue UK also worked on it.

The next stage will look at tailoring simulator training to each trainee and measuring stress and mental workload. It will also test whether skills learned in the simulator carry over to real rescues. [The full report](https://repository.essex.ac.uk/44177/) is on the university's website.
points: Up to 92% of trainee evaluations reported learning something new or sharpening skills
Crews can rehearse winch failures and engine failures safely

courts.headline: Harlow hospital gets coroner warning over resuscitation decisions
courts.summary: A coroner's report says staff at the Princess Alexandra Hospital do not fully understand the rules on do not resuscitate decisions. The hospital has replied, setting out the changes it is making.
body: An Essex coroner has written to the Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow with concerns about decisions on resuscitation and mental capacity. Assistant coroner Stephen Simblet issued a prevention of future deaths report after the death of Luciana Gianfrancesco, 52, at the hospital. It went to the hospital trust and to Essex Partnership University NHS Foundation Trust (EPUT), which provided her mental health care. The report is dated 2 July 2026 and was published by the Courts and Tribunals Judiciary on 12 November.

The report says she died after being admitted with pneumonia and other health problems. It says doctors decided in April 2024 that she had capacity to refuse treatment. Her family and supported living staff disagreed. The report says this led to some delays in life-saving treatment, which she later agreed to have. It also says a do not resuscitate form was partly filled in by one doctor. Neither her family nor the consultant in charge knew about it, and no senior doctor signed it off.

The coroner raised three concerns. Staff are unsure how to assess capacity when a patient does not always accept life-saving treatment, and how to get advice from psychiatric staff. Clinical staff do not fully understand or follow the steps for making, recording and sharing do not resuscitate decisions. And it is not clear whether the hospital's resuscitation policies meet national standards for patients who are clinically obese. The inquest has not finished. It was adjourned after most of the evidence was heard, while more evidence on resuscitation is gathered.

In its formal reply to the coroner, dated 18 August and published alongside the report, the trust accepts there were shortcomings in how the do not resuscitate decision was documented and recorded. Its own policy says such a form must be endorsed by the patient's consultant within 48 hours, and that did not happen. The trust's cardiac arrest review panel found the records did not show the reasoning behind the decision or how the benefits and burdens of resuscitation had been weighed, and that the decision was not formally reviewed when one of the reasons for it, a high potassium level, improved.

The letter, signed by the trust's chief executive, chief medical officer and interim chief nursing officer, says a digital system for recording resuscitation and treatment escalation decisions, known as ReSPECT, is now in use across the hospital. Staff have been told that obesity or any other single condition must never on its own justify a do not resuscitate decision, and that a mental health diagnosis does not by itself mean a patient lacks capacity. The trust plans more training on resuscitation decisions and the Mental Capacity Act, clearer guidance on when to ask for specialist mental health advice, and continued audits. The letter gives no dates for these steps and has no separate answer on the coroner's concern about resuscitation policies for clinically obese patients.
points: Trust accepts the form was not signed off by a consultant within 48 hours
Digital system for recording resuscitation decisions now in use
The inquest will resume once further evidence on resuscitation is in

official.headline: Southend names Nigel Folkard Honorary Alderman
official.summary: Southend's councillors also gave certificates to a dance school, a powerlifter and the Masonic centre at Saxon Hall.
body: Nigel Folkard has been made an Honorary Alderman of Southend-on-Sea for his service to the council, awarded by councillors at an extraordinary council meeting on Thursday 26 November. Southend-on-Sea City Council announced the honours the next morning.

The same evening, Frank Banks and Councillor David Garston were granted the Freedom of the City, [as The Seax reported](/story/southend-united-frankie-banks-freedom-of-the-city/). At full council the Mayor, Councillor Tony Cox, presented certificates of recognition. Expressions Theatre Arts Dance School was honoured after being named National Dance School of the Year at the National Entertainment Awards 2026, and powerlifter Will Thorogood for his national competition results.

Saxon Hall, the Southend Masonic Centre, was recognised for its long service to the community, and five council officers were thanked for their work on the recent Southend Business Show. Youth Mayor Apryl Banoss and Deputy Youth Mayor Hannah Korsten-Woodward received their chains of office and spoke to councillors about the Youth Council's work.
points: Expressions named National Dance School of the Year
Youth Mayor Apryl Banoss given her chain of office
Five council officers thanked for the Business Show
official.newAngle: Nigel Folkard made Honorary Alderman and certificates of recognition presented at the same meetings.

official.headline: Basildon end-terrace house destroyed by fire as crews protect neighbours
official.summary: An end-terrace house in Basildon was completely alight when firefighters arrived. Smoke spread to the home next door.
body: Firefighters were called to a house fire in Basildon at 5.57pm on Thursday 26 November, Essex County Fire and Rescue Service said. Crews found the end-terrace house completely alight when they arrived, with smoke drifting into the neighbouring property.
Crews put the fire out and worked to limit the damage to the homes either side. The fire service has not said whether anyone was hurt or how many people lived at the house.
The cause of the fire is now being investigated.

Residents and community groups can apply for money for sport sessions, walking and cycling groups, fitness classes and activities for older people. The council says it especially wants ideas that help people of all ages and abilities who find it hard to take part.

Councillor Dr Tim Barrett, who chairs the council's housing, health and community committee, said the grants were "a fantastic opportunity" for local groups. Details and the application form are on the council's Active Brentwood page.

body: Crews were called to the house in Colchester at 12.35pm on Tuesday 24 November and found the kitchen heavily smoke-logged, Essex County Fire and Rescue Service said. The fire was out by 1pm.

Firefighter Chris Simson, from Colchester Fire Station, said the neighbours "acted quickly" when they heard the alarms. Crews then knocked on doors nearby to give fire safety advice and carried out two home safety visits. The service fits smoke alarms free for people who need them: book at essex-fire.gov.uk/book or call 0300 303 0088.

body: It was 4.27am when crews were sent to the house, after the residents' smoke alarms went off and woke them, Essex County Fire and Rescue Service said. The fire had started in a log burner. Firefighters had it out by 5.51am.

Watch Manager Kris Mortimer, from Tollesbury Fire Station, said: "Incidents like this show why it's so important to have working smoke alarms at home. Thankfully, the smoke alarms went off and woke the residents up. If they didn't have them, it could have been a very different incident."

The fire service advises having at least one working smoke alarm on every floor of a home and testing it once a month. Anyone without working alarms can contact the service at essex-fire.gov.uk/book or on 0300 303 0088.

body: Two men, aged 19 and 25, were arrested on suspicion of grievous bodily harm after a man in his 30s was seriously assaulted in Market Row, Saffron Walden, Essex Police said. Officers were called at about 1.40am on Sunday 15 November.

Police said the man was attacked by a number of people and suffered several facial injuries. He was taken to hospital, and his injuries are not thought to be life-threatening. The two men were arrested on the Sunday afternoon and taken into custody for questioning.

Officers want to hear from anyone who saw an altercation earlier on the Saturday evening inside the Nexus Lounge on Market Hill, which they believe may be linked. Anyone with information or footage can contact Essex Police online or on 101, quoting incident 81 of 15 November.

body: A passer-by dialled 999 at 9.36pm on Tuesday 17 November after spotting a narrowboat on fire on the River Lee near Dobbs Weir Road in Roydon. By the time Essex County Fire and Rescue Service crews arrived, the boat was fully alight.

About 20 firefighters, some of them on-call firefighters who live or work within five minutes of their stations, worked to put the fire out. The fire service said no one was aboard the boat at the time.
Crews left the scene at 12.43am on Wednesday 18 November, and the fire service says an investigation will be carried out to establish the cause.

body: More than 300 people went to Epping Forest District Council's Tourism and Hospitality Job Fair at the Civic Offices in Epping on Thursday 12 November, the council said on Wednesday 18 November. Visitors looking for work, a change of career, seasonal jobs or apprenticeships met employers face to face.

The council ran the fair with the Department for Work and Pensions. Exhibitors included Epping Forest District Museum, Princess Alexandra Hospital's catering service, Lee Valley Regional Park, the Royal Gunpowder Mills, Harlow College, Visit Essex and Delta Hotels by Marriott.

Councillor Holly Whitbread, the council's portfolio holder for economic development, said tourism and hospitality offer careers for people of all ages and backgrounds, and that the event helped bring businesses and jobseekers together.

body: Colchester City Council opened its consultation on the 2027/28 budget on Monday 16 November, asking residents where it should cut, spend more or work differently. It names rising costs, steady demand for services and the growing cost of supporting people facing homelessness as the main pressures.

Councillor William Sunnucks, portfolio holder for resources, said: "We need your views on where we can save money." The answers will shape priorities for services including bin collections, parks, leisure, housing and community safety. People can fill in the online survey or attend a Residents' Panel session at the Town Hall from 10am to noon on Tuesday 8 December, or from 7pm to 8.30pm on Thursday 10 December.
Cabinet looks at the first draft budget position on Wednesday 2 December, and the consultation closes at 9am on Monday 14 December. Full Council sets the final budget in February 2027.

stories.summary: Witham Town are now in the Isthmian North play-off places. Brightlingsea Regent had a tough night at the new leaders.
body: Witham Town won 2-0 away at Takeley in the Isthmian League North Division on Tuesday 24 November. It was their second away win in four days, after a 3-1 victory at AFC Sudbury on the Saturday. Witham now sit sixth with 29 points from 17 games. Takeley slip to 18th, one place above the relegation zone.

Brightlingsea Regent lost 4-1 at Cambridge City on the same evening. The Cambridge Independent reported that Fletcher Toll opened the scoring after 31 minutes. Charlie Royle added two more and Freddie Hockey got the other. City manager Mickey Spillane said Regent scored from their only shot, a breakaway. The win took City top, while Regent stay 21st on 15 points.

There were Essex winners in the Velocity Cup too. Brentwood Town beat Bowers & Pitsea 4-2 at home, and Maldon & Tiptree won 4-3 at Buckhurst Hill. In the Isthmian Premier Division, Aveley lost 3-1 at Eastbourne Borough. Witham are at home to Gorleston on Saturday, and Brightlingsea go to Mulbarton Wanderers.

body: Aveley lost 3-1 away to Eastbourne Borough in the Isthmian Premier Division on Tuesday 24 November. The win lifted Eastbourne back up to third. Aveley stay 14th, with 23 points from 18 games.

Freddie Carter put the home side ahead in the 25th minute, shortly after Romel Aarons-Royal hit the woodwork for Aveley. Matt Johnson levelled for the visitors before the break. Josh Rees restored the lead on the stroke of half-time, and Kai Corbett made it three four minutes into the second half. Eastbourne also had a goal ruled out by the assistant referee's flag.
Your Thurrock noted that November has brought Aveley two league wins, two league defeats and exits from two cups. Their next game is away to AFC Whyteleafe on Saturday.
points: Eastbourne goalkeeper Lewis Carey denied Malachi Napa and Anthony Jeffery
Eastbourne waved away penalty appeals early in the second half
Next: AFC Whyteleafe away, 3pm kick-off

stories.headline: Essex to open 2027 T20 season at Hove, with six games in Chelmsford
stories.summary: Essex Cricket has published next summer's T20 fixtures for its men and women. Members can book first, from 2 December.
body: Essex men's side will start the 2027 Vitality Blast away to Sussex Sharks at Hove on Friday 21 May, Essex Cricket announced on Wednesday 25 November. Their first home game is the Kent Spitfires derby at the Ambassador Cruise Line Ground in Chelmsford a week later. The club bills that match as the first part of its 'Battle of the Bridge'.

Sky Sports reported that the competition keeps three groups of six counties. Essex are in Group C with Kent, Hampshire, Middlesex, Surrey and Sussex. Each county plays 12 group games, six of them at home. Essex's other Chelmsford dates are Middlesex on 30 May, Surrey on 4 June, Sussex on 27 June, Hampshire on 2 July and Warwickshire Bears on 4 July.

Group winners and runners-up go through to the quarter-finals, along with the two best third-placed sides. Men's Finals Day is at Edgbaston on Saturday 17 July, and the women's Finals Day is at Trent Bridge the next day. Essex Women begin away to Surrey at The Kia Oval on 23 May. Their first home game is against Glamorgan on 30 May, as a double-header with the men's Middlesex match.
## Tickets

Members get the first chance to book, in a priority window from 2 December. Passes covering every Blast fixture go on sale on 9 December, and general sale opens on 17 February. Essex Cricket said single match tickets will be released in due course.
points: Group C: Essex, Kent, Hampshire, Middlesex, Surrey, Sussex
Last group game: Middlesex at Lord's on 11 July
General sale opens on 17 February

stories.headline: Southend climb to fourth with 2-0 win at Forest Green
stories.summary: Southend United won 2-0 at The New Lawn on Tuesday 24 November, bouncing back from their home defeat by leaders Boreham Wood four days earlier.
body: Harry Cardwell and Kyle McAdam scored after a goalless first half. Nine minutes after the break a cleared corner fell to McAdam just outside the box. He drove it through a crowded area and Cardwell got the slightest of touches to put Southend ahead. Twenty minutes later two substitutes combined: Sahid Kamara ran at the defence and found Zavier Massiah-Edwards, who teed up McAdam to finish into the far corner.

Forest Green had chances of their own in front of 1,498. Southend goalkeeper Joe Duncan saved from Jayden Clarke at close range, and Clarke later saw a deflected shot hit the outside of the post. At the other end, Forest Green keeper Pagel kept out a header from McAdam and a shot from substitute Promise Omochere.

The win takes Southend to fourth in the National League on 35 points, level with Yeovil Town and Harrogate Town, after the night's other results on Sky Sports. Leaders Boreham Wood are 13 points clear. Southend's next home game is against Dartford at Roots Hall.
points: Cardwell and McAdam scored 20 minutes apart

Boreham Wood lead the table by 13 points

stories.summary: Grays Athletic have brought back a former manager in a new boardroom role. He left in February with the Thurrock club fighting relegation.
body: Grays Athletic announced on Monday 23 November that Darren Manning, the club's first-team manager for three years, is returning as director of football, Your Thurrock reported. He will work with chairman Lee Vehit and vice-chairman Gavin Holland on recruitment, player development and links with the club's Community Academy.
Lewis Clark has managed the Isthmian North side since October, when Mitch Hahn and Ash Miller left.

stories.headline: Chelmsford City climb into play-offs as Barham penalty beats Maidstone
stories.summary: Former Stones striker Jack Barham scored for the third time in two days as City edged a tight Monday night game.
body: Chelmsford City moved up to seventh in National League South, and into the play-off places, after a 1-0 win over Maidstone United at the EMG Inspire Stadium on Monday night. Jack Barham scored the only goal from the penalty spot ten minutes after half-time, sending Lenny Holden the wrong way against the club he used to play for.

It was Barham's third goal in two days. He scored twice at Walton & Hersham on Saturday, when City were pegged back to 2-2 by two late goals. Manager Mark Cooper made two changes for the visit of the Stones, bringing back Leo Sery and captain Cav Miley.

Maidstone were much the better side early on. Ben Tompkins was booked inside three minutes for bringing down Riley Court on the edge of the box, and Court's free kick went just past the post. Jayden Davis then lobbed a shot onto the crossbar and Stan Leech headed the rebound wide.

City's goalkeeper Alfie Marriott kept them level, diving to keep out Court and pushing a fierce Dermi Lusala strike wide. The home side grew into the game, and Sery forced a save from Holden from close range after 31 minutes before an Ashley Clarke shot took a double deflection and flew just wide. Sery also went down in the box in first-half stoppage time, but the referee waved play on.

The penalty came in the 55th minute after a foul in the Maidstone area, and Leo Hamblin was booked soon afterwards. Maidstone pushed for an equaliser but managed little, with Noah Nzuzi's low shot from distance held by Marriott with 13 minutes left and Lusala firing wide in stoppage time.

The result was a second 1-0 defeat in three days for Maidstone, who had lost at Farnham Town on Saturday. Maidstone's own report said they were made to pay for failing to take the chances they created in the first half.
points: Alfie Marriott made the key saves, from Court and Lusala before the break
A crowd of 1,421 watched, with Ayrton Hursey refereeing
Four Chelmsford players were booked, to Maidstone's one

stories.headline: Colchester United lose 2-1 at Tranmere to 90th-minute winner
stories.summary: Dylan Jones struck at the death at Prenton Park after Sean Raggett had cancelled out Tom Ince's opener for the U's.
body: Colchester United were beaten by Tranmere Rovers in League Two at Prenton Park, Birkenhead, on Saturday 21 November, with the home side's winner coming in the 90th minute. It ends a short lift for Danny Cowley's side, who had beaten Gillingham 2-0 a week earlier for their first league win since the end of August.

Tranmere had the better of the opening stages and went ahead shortly before the half-hour mark, when Ince, back in Darrell Clarke's starting line-up, picked up a loose ball, drove forward and finished. Colchester were level just before the break as Raggett scored from a Jack Payne cross, and the sides went in at 1-1. Jones then won it for Tranmere in the final minute of normal time.

Colchester went into the game 21st in League Two, three points above the relegation zone, and stay on 15 points. York City are next, at the JobServe Community Stadium on Saturday 28 November at 3pm. The U's then travel to Grimsby Town the following Tuesday. Mansfield Town visit in the FA Cup second round on Saturday 5 December.
points: Tranmere had lost 1-0 at Fleetwood a week earlier
Ince came in for Lee O'Connor in the only Tranmere change
York City visit Colchester next

stories.headline: Shrimpers lose five-goal table-top thriller
stories.summary: Tyreece Simpson and debutant Rico Richards struck two minutes apart after the break, but the Shrimpers could not complete the comeback against the runaway leaders.
body: Southend United lost 3-2 to Boreham Wood, the runaway National League leaders, at Roots Hall on Friday 20 November. The Shrimpers fought back from three goals down but fell one short.

Boreham Wood were 3-0 up by the 33rd minute, with a former Southend player among the scorers. Oliver Bainbridge finished inside the near post on 19 minutes. Ben Whitfield converted at the far post 10 minutes later, and Regan Booty set up both. Ex-Shrimper Zak Brunt then slammed in from close range from Whitfield's pass.

Southend made three changes at half-time, sending on Maxwell McKnight, Tyreece Simpson and Anthony Hartigan for Leon Chambers-Parillon, Omari Patrick and Zavier Massiah-Edwards. Simpson headed in McKnight's cross on 65 minutes. Two minutes later Rico Richards fired in off the far post from Promise Omochere's pass. He was making his debut, having come on for Oliver Coker just before the hour.

Roots Hall roared for an equaliser through the remaining 23 minutes and four minutes of added time, but it never came. Southend were shown six yellow cards, to Omochere, Daniel Cox, Ben Goodliffe, Simpson, Hartigan and Darren Oldaker.
Head coach Kieron Dyer was back in the dugout after a one-match touchline ban for a game shown live on DAZN.
Boreham Wood's 15th league win of the season stretched their unbeaten start to 18 matches and moved them 13 points clear at the top of the National League.
points: A crowd of 9,985 was at Roots Hall
Former Shrimper Zak Brunt scored Boreham Wood's third
Six Southend players were booked

stories.headline: Chelmsford City captain Cav Miley falls down badger hole in training
stories.summary: Manager Mark Cooper said the fall affected Miley's game as the Clarets let a two-goal lead slip at Walton & Hersham.
points: Jack Barham scored twice before half-time on Saturday
The hosts hit back with two goals in three minutes
Miley won the FA Trophy at Wembley in his last game for Southend
body: Chelmsford City captain Cav Miley played through Saturday's 2-2 draw at Walton & Hersham after falling down a badger hole in training, manager Mark Cooper has revealed.

Cooper said in his [post-match interview](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=QWkvdR4TEJk) that the mishap had affected the midfielder's performance. Miley still played the full game in Surrey on Saturday 21 November.

It was an afternoon of two halves for the Clarets. Jack Barham put them ahead on 27 minutes, slotting under goalkeeper Dillon Addai after Ash Clarke and Cam Green combined, and doubled the lead three minutes before the break from Clarke's outside-of-the-boot pass. They were his sixth and seventh league goals of the season.

Walton & Hersham hit back late. Makise Evans pulled one back on 80 minutes, and substitute Kleyton Dowglas De Biazze Junior equalised three minutes later. A crowd of 576 watched the National League South game, which came a week after City's FA Trophy exit at AFC Telford United.

Miley, 31, joined Chelmsford from Southend United in the summer on a two-year deal. He was Southend's player of the year in his first season, when he did not miss a game, and won the FA Trophy at Wembley in his last game for the Shrimpers. He began his career at Jersey side St Pauls while working as an electrician, before turning professional with Eastleigh at 22.

Torquay's Jacob Beaumont-Clark hit the base of the post before half-time, and a Braintree defender cleared a Sonny Blu Lo-Everton shot off the line. Braintree's best chance came late on, when Harry Shield cleared Alex Bolovan's effort off the line.

stories.headline: Essex football fixtures: Colchester go to Tranmere on Saturday
stories.summary: Three Isthmian North Division games are all-Essex derbies, while Billericay Town and Chelmsford City face the two bottom clubs in the National League South.
body: Colchester United lead the Essex fixtures on Saturday 21 November 2026 with a League Two trip to Tranmere Rovers at Prenton Park, kick-off 3pm. Southend United are not in action after losing 3-2 at home to National League leaders Boreham Wood on Friday 20 November.

Colchester defender Ellis Iandolo had stitches in an ear injury and could wear headgear, and Sean Raggett has been kept from heading the ball in training. Danny Cowley hoped both would be available. Striker Kylian Kouassi is still out with a hamstring injury.

In the National League South, sixth-placed Billericay Town host bottom club Slough Town, and Chelmsford City travel to Walton & Hersham, who are 23rd. Braintree Town welcome Torquay United to Cressing Road. Torquay's preview says Braintree's Ben Isaacson is an injury concern after being forced off with a collision, while Torquay are without Tegan Finn. All three games kick off at 3pm.
In the Isthmian Premier Division, Aveley go to Carshalton Athletic, Maldon & Tiptree visit Chatham Town and Brentwood Town are away at Wingate & Finchley. Stanway Rovers host Burgess Hill Town.

The Isthmian North Division has three Essex derbies: Brightlingsea Regent against Grays Athletic, Canvey Island against Buckhurst Hill, and Takeley against Concord Rangers. Bowers & Pitsea host Felixstowe & Walton United, Little Oakley play Hashtag United, Tilbury take on Wroxham and Witham Town travel to AFC Sudbury. Every Isthmian game kicks off at 3pm.

stories.headline: Essex all-rounder Luc Benkenstein leaves for Durham
stories.summary: The leg-spinner has left by mutual agreement after 80 appearances across all formats since joining in 2021.
body: Luc Benkenstein has left Essex by mutual agreement and will join Durham as part of the deal, the club announced on Thursday 19 November.

The all-rounder arrived at Chelmsford in 2021 and made his debut that season in the One Day Cup, against Durham. He went on to play 80 times for Essex across all formats, and had signed a contract extension that ran until the end of the 2027 season.

His father, former South Africa international Dale Benkenstein, was appointed a batting consultant at Durham in March. Essex thanked Benkenstein for his efforts and commitment and wished him well for the future.
points: Debut came against his new county

stories.headline: Aveley out of Velocity Cup after 4-3 defeat at Cheshunt
stories.summary: The Thurrock club were one of three Essex sides knocked out of the Isthmian League cup in the third round, with Stanway Rovers and Grays Athletic both beaten 3-0.
body: Aveley went 2-0 down inside 20 minutes against Cheshunt at Theobalds Lane on Tuesday 17 November 2026, after goals from Tommy Wood and Raul Fernandes Da Silva. Kymani Thomas replied on 28 minutes and, after Kenny Coker's penalty, Anthony Jeffrey made it 3-2 in the last minute of the first half, Your Thurrock reports.

Joe Re restored Cheshunt's two-goal cushion on 51 minutes. Thomas struck again on 66 minutes, but the Millers could not find a leveller and lose their grip on the Alan Turvey Trophy, which they last won in 2023. Jamie Grossart was back in goal and William Turner-Smith made his debut.

Stanway Rovers lost at Dulwich Hamlet in front of 414 at Champion Hill, where Amadou Kassarate and Michael Chambers were among the scorers, and Grays Athletic were beaten at Newmarket Town. All three are back in league action on Saturday 21 November: Aveley at Carshalton Athletic, Stanway at home to Burgess Hill Town and Grays at Brightlingsea Regent.
points: Kymani Thomas scored twice for Aveley

stories.headline: Billericay Town hold Truro City to goalless draw in Cornwall
stories.summary: Billericay Town stay sixth in the National League South after taking a point in wet and windy conditions against one of the division's front-runners.
body: Billericay Town drew 0-0 at Truro City in the National League South on Tuesday 17 November 2026, watched by 1,460 at Truro City Stadium. Both defences had to clear shots off their own line.

Truro forward Luke Jephcott saw an eighth-minute effort scrambled away after a Christian Oxlade-Chamberlain long throw, and a Will Dean header from a set piece was also cleared on the line. After the break the home attack rarely troubled teenage Billericay goalkeeper Khari Ranson, and late on Jephcott tracked back to stop Jamie Mauge from shooting.

The result keeps Truro fourth, four points behind leaders Ebbsfleet United with a game in hand, The Post reported. Billericay host Slough Town on Saturday 21 November before a trip to Ebbsfleet on Tuesday 24 November.

body: Scrivens will captain the side at the Wankhede Stadium, Essex County Cricket Club announced on Tuesday 17 November. England Women A have split the captaincy across the three formats of the multi-format tour.

Surrey bowler Ryana MacDonald-Gay will lead the team in the three-match T20 series that opens the tour in Pune. Surrey wicketkeeper-batter Kira Chathli takes charge for the three 50-over matches in Mumbai, as she did in the home series last summer.
Injuries have forced two squad changes.

stories.headline: Brentwood Town lose 3-0 at home to Ramsgate in Isthmian Premier
stories.summary: All three goals came before half-time at the Brentwood club's ground, and a second-half penalty save stopped the margin growing.
body: Brentwood Town lost 3-0 at home to Ramsgate at the Brentwood Arena on Saturday 14 November 2026 in the Isthmian League Premier Division, while Stanway Rovers drew 0-0 at Lewes. The defeat leaves Brentwood nineteenth on 16 points, and Stanway sit twenty-first on nine.

Ramsgate led inside two minutes when Raphe Brown headed in after Brentwood goalkeeper Aiden Prall had saved a Billy Munday header. Alfie Paxman struck from the edge of the area for the second, then set up Callum Jones for the third before the break. Prall kept the margin down by stopping a Paxman penalty shortly before the hour.

At The Dripping Pan, Stanway followed a goalless home draw with Whitehawk a week earlier with another shut-out, a result that lifted them off the bottom of the division. Brentwood travel to Burgess Hill Town on Tuesday 17 November, with a 19:45 kick-off, and Stanway host Burgess Hill on Saturday 21 November.

Grant Bartlett, Tom Soar and Hallden Barnes-Garner scored in the first two periods. After Paddison's goal, Ollie Baldock converted on the power play and Josh Batch, named man of the match, found an empty net with 14 seconds left.

stories.headline: Billericay Town beat Waltham Abbey to stay in the FA Trophy
stories.summary: Billericay are the last Essex club left in non-league's national knockout competition, after a weekend that ended the cup hopes of Braintree, Aveley and Chelmsford City.
body: Billericay Town won the all-Essex FA Trophy second round tie against Waltham Abbey 3-1 at New Lodge on Saturday 14 November 2026. Elsewhere, Braintree Town lost 3-2 at home to Kettering Town and Aveley went down by the same score at Walton & Hersham.

At Cressing Road, Shaun Jeffers gave Kettering an early lead before Alfie Lewis levelled on 36 minutes. Lewis Coyle restored the visitors' advantage early in the second half and Ben Isaacson equalised again, but Jaiden White struck what proved the winner on 64 minutes. Isaacson and Kettering's Edward Panter were both forced off injured after a collision in the 82nd minute.

Chelmsford City also went out, losing 6-5 on penalties after a 1-1 draw at AFC Telford United. Braintree's own report notes the club has now exited all four of its cup competitions this season, leaving manager Steve Pitt's side to concentrate on the National League South.
points: Braintree's crowd against Kettering was 407

stories.headline: Southend United fight back to beat ten-man Aldershot Town 2-1 at Roots Hall
stories.summary: Second-half goals from Kyle McAdam and Tyreece Simpson kept Southend in the National League play-off places.
body: Southend United came from behind to beat Aldershot Town 2-1 in the National League at Roots Hall, Southend-on-Sea, on Saturday 14 November 2026. Anisius Lewis gave the visitors a sixth-minute lead, and Aldershot played most of the game with ten men after John Gilbert was sent off on 26 minutes. McAdam equalised on 56 minutes and Simpson scored the winner on 66.
points: Southend are third in the National League on 32 points

stories.headline: Canvey Island hit five at Witham Town in Isthmian North
stories.summary: Bowers & Pitsea also won at Concord Rangers on a strong Saturday for Essex sides on the road, with Tilbury and Brightlingsea Regent collecting away wins too.
body: Canvey Island won 5-1 at Witham Town in the Isthmian League North Division on Saturday 14 November 2026, in front of 413 at Spa Road. In the other Essex derby, Bowers & Pitsea beat Concord Rangers 2-1 at Thames Road.

Tilbury won 4-0 at Felixstowe & Walton United and Brightlingsea Regent won 3-1 at Wroxham. Buckhurst Hill beat AFC Sudbury 2-1 at home, while Takeley drew 1-1 at Fakenham Town and Grays Athletic lost 3-1 to leaders Gorleston.
points: Gorleston lead the division on 37 points
Concord Rangers are seventh, the highest Essex club

stories.headline: Chelmsford City knocked out of the FA Trophy on penalties at AFC Telford United
stories.summary: The Clarets were beaten 6-5 in a shootout in Shropshire despite two saves from goalkeeper Marriott.
body: Chelmsford City went out of the FA Trophy second round at AFC Telford United on Saturday 14 November 2026 after a 1-1 draw. Green put City ahead on 20 minutes with a 40-yard strike that went in off the post, before Cawthorne levelled for Telford on 35 minutes. A late Tompkins header was ruled out for a foul, and Crowther sent the decisive kick over the bar as Telford won 6-5 on penalties.
points: Attendance: 1,031
Green went off injured at half-time
Ben Worman made his debut on loan from Solihull Moors

stories.headline: Colchester United end 10-game winless run by beating Gillingham 2-0
stories.summary: Two goals inside nine second-half minutes at the JobServe Community Stadium lifted the mood in Colchester after weeks without a win.
body: Colchester United beat Gillingham 2-0 in League Two at the JobServe Community Stadium on Saturday 14 November 2026. Jack Payne converted a 61st-minute penalty after being fouled by Brophy, and Harry Anderson finished from close range around 74 minutes. A crowd of 5,548, including 1,255 from Kent, watched the U's end a run of 10 games without a win.
points: Visiting goalkeeper Ollie Wright saved from Anderson before half-time
Referee Lewis Sandoe waved away a Gillingham penalty appeal
Gillingham suffered their fifth league defeat of the season

stories.headline: Southend United sign former Tottenham academy defender Maxwell McKnight
stories.summary: The 22-year-old, who played for Brentford B last season, went straight into Kieron Dyer's starting line-up against Aldershot Town on Saturday 14 November.
body: Southend United also hold an option to keep McKnight for a further 12 months, BBC Sport reports. He came through the academy at Tottenham Hotspur but never made a first-team appearance there.
points: Club holds a 12-month extension option
No first-team games at Tottenham

stories.headline: Essex Senior Cup quarter-final draw sets holders Billericay Town's path
stories.summary: Witham Town could meet Colchester United, and Aveley host Hullbridge Sports, in the last eight of the BBC Essex Senior Cup.
body: Billericay Town, who beat Little Oakley 7-0 in the last round, will play Redbridge or Grays Athletic in the quarter-finals; those two clubs meet on Monday 23 November. Witham Town face Colchester United or Hashtag United, who play their tie on Tuesday 17 November, Your Thurrock reports.
Stanway are in the quarter-finals for the first time, and Hullbridge Sports for the first time in 17 years. BBC Essex's Victoria Polley drew the home clubs on Friday 13 November.

stories.headline: Essex fixtures: Colchester host Gillingham on Saturday 14 November
stories.summary: Southend United face Aldershot Town, Billericay Town and Waltham Abbey meet in an all-Essex FA Trophy tie, and there are two derbies in the Isthmian North.
body: Colchester United and Southend United are both at home on Saturday 14 November 2026, with 3pm kick-offs. Colchester play Gillingham in League Two at the JobServe Community Stadium, and Southend take on Aldershot Town in the National League at Roots Hall.

Fans going to Roots Hall should know that Essex Police brought in a dispersal order across central Southend from 9am. The city's Christmas lights switch-on is also today, so the centre is expected to be busy.

Five Essex clubs are in the FA Trophy second round, with kick-off times still to be confirmed. Chelmsford City travel to AFC Telford United and Braintree Town host Kettering Town. Aveley go to Walton & Hersham. Billericay Town's home tie with Waltham Abbey guarantees one Essex side a place in the next round.
In the Isthmian Premier Division, Brentwood Town host Ramsgate at the Brentwood Centre Arena and Stanway Rovers make the trip to Lewes.

The Isthmian North Division derbies are Concord Rangers against Bowers & Pitsea at Thames Road on Canvey Island, and Witham Town against Canvey Island at Spa Road. Grays Athletic host Gorleston and Buckhurst Hill welcome AFC Sudbury, while Takeley, Tilbury and Brightlingsea Regent are away at Fakenham Town, Felixstowe & Walton United and Wroxham. All kick off at 3pm.

In rugby union, Westcliff host Hertford in Regional 1 South East and Harlow are away at Woodford. On Sunday evening, Chelmsford Chieftains play Slough Jets in the ice hockey Challenge Cup at Riverside Ice and Leisure in Chelmsford, starting at 6pm.
points: Chelmsford City face a long trip to Shropshire in the FA Trophy
Westcliff's rugby game against Hertford starts at 2pm
Colchester and Southend have both posted match previews on their club websites

stories.headline: Aveley cruise past Hutton 5-0 in the BBC Essex Senior Cup fourth round
stories.summary: Aveley's Isthmian Premier side were far too strong for their Essex Senior League hosts, with two substitutes scoring late on.
body: Aveley won 5-0 away to Hutton in the BBC Essex Senior Cup on Wednesday 11 November 2026, at Billericay's New Lodge stadium. Harry Critchley headed the first goal on 29 minutes and Francis Mampolo added a second early in the second half.
Shad Ngandu made it three before Said Mariche pounced on a goalkeeping error on 88 minutes and Alejandro Machado, also on from the bench, scored in the final minute.
points: Five different Aveley players found the net

Mampolo struck within five minutes of the restart

stories.headline: Braintree Town beaten 2-0 at Salisbury despite facing ten men after half-time
stories.summary: The Braintree side had an extra man for the whole second half in Wiltshire but could not find a goal in the National League South.
body: Braintree Town lost 2-0 away to Salisbury in the National League South on Tuesday 10 November 2026 at the Raymond McEnhill Stadium.
Mo Dabre put the hosts ahead on 20 minutes before Malachi Ogunleye was sent off in first-half stoppage time. Nathan Odokonyero settled it on 63 minutes, three minutes after coming off the bench.

stories.summary: The Thurrock side, short of several players through cup-tie rules and absences, bowed out of the county competition in the fourth round.
body: Tilbury lost 2-0 to National League South side Dagenham & Redbridge in the fourth round of the BBC Essex Senior Cup on Tuesday 10 November 2026. Freddie Ingram put the visitors ahead in the seventh minute after a defensive mistake, and Wiktor Makowski converted a 75th-minute penalty.
Dagenham played most of the tie a man down after Jack Bateson was shown a straight red card on 30 minutes for a last-man foul on Rasheed Salau.

Paul Digby, Milton Oni, Jaden Williams and Adrian Akande scored their spot-kicks, while Lo-Tutala saved from Steven Turner and Josh Pitts.

Tom Soar and Sasha Maltsev both scored twice, with Hallden Barnes-Garner, Grant Bartlett, Daniel Hitchings, Lane Paddison and Rio Grinell-Parke also on target.

stories.summary: Barnes scored twice for the National League South leaders, but the Clarets twice hit back in front of 1,390 fans.
body: Chelmsford City drew 2-2 with National League South leaders Ebbsfleet United at the Dunmow Group Community Stadium on Monday night. Barnes put Ebbsfleet ahead on 33 minutes, Ash Clarke levelled two minutes later and Jack Barham headed City in front from a Manny Egbo cross on 52 minutes.
Barnes equalised on 68 minutes, and both sides pushed for a winner, with keeper Marriott saving late on. The crowd was 1,390.

stories.headline: Maldon & Tiptree win 3-1 at Wingate & Finchley
stories.summary: Aveley were beaten 4-0 at Ramsgate on a mixed Saturday for the Essex clubs in the Isthmian Premier Division, which also brought two draws.
body: Maldon & Tiptree produced the best Essex result of the day in the Isthmian Premier Division, winning 3-1 away at Wingate & Finchley on Saturday. Brentwood Town came away from Three Bridges with a 1-1 draw, while Stanway Rovers and Whitehawk finished goalless.

Aveley had a much harder afternoon, losing 4-0 at promotion-chasing Ramsgate in front of a crowd of 1,444. Billy Munday headed the hosts in front inside two minutes from an Alfie Paxman corner, and Rowan Liburd made it two on 15 minutes after Aveley goalkeeper Jamie Grossart dropped the ball at his feet. Paxman added a third on 77 minutes and Latrell Lewis struck in the 90th, while Ramsgate keeper Jonny Henly also saved a penalty from Malachi Napa.

The defeat leaves Aveley fifteenth in the table. Their next game is away at Hutton in the Essex Senior Cup on Wednesday 11 November, and they return to league action at Carshalton on Saturday 21 November.

stories.headline: Braintree Town beaten 4-1 by Weston-super-Mare in National League South
stories.summary: Luke Coulson struck twice before half-time for the hosts at the Optima Stadium, and Hubbard's late goal was only a consolation for the Iron.
body: Braintree Town suffered a heavy 4-1 defeat away to Weston-super-Mare in the National League South on Saturday. The Iron were three goals down within eight minutes of the restart and could not find a way back.

Weston had a goal from Ollie Hulbert ruled out for offside before Luke Coulson opened the scoring from around 30 yards with a deflected effort on 33 minutes. Coulson then converted a penalty on the stroke of half-time after Will Jenkins Davies was tripped, Hulbert made it three on 53 minutes and Jenkins Davies added a fourth six minutes later.
Hubbard pulled a goal back for Braintree on 86 minutes, and Louis Britton dragged a late one-on-one chance over the bar for the home side. The game was watched by a crowd of 962.

Before the first-round tie, midfielder Paul Digby, 31 and back in the Colchester side, told the Gazette the players knew how big the game was for Worcester. He has plenty of experience of the competition, including a third-round upset, and said he loves the FA Cup.

Grant Bartlett, Lane Paddison twice and Sasha Maltsev twice scored for the Chieftains. Maltsev's second goal came while Chelmsford were shorthanded, and he was named the visitors' man of the match.
The sides were level at 1-1 after the first period, and Swindon held a 4-3 lead going into the third before Chelmsford drew level at 5-5.

stories.summary: Danny Scopes' side twice found the net through their striker and held on for a point against the Daggers in the National League South.
body: Billericay Town came away from Dagenham & Redbridge with a 2-2 draw in the National League South on Saturday. Elliot Long scored both goals for Billericay, who had to dig in after the break to protect a share of the points.

Long put Billericay ahead on 27 minutes before Henry Hawkins levelled for the hosts three minutes before half-time. Beautyman then gave Dagenham the lead from the penalty spot on 55 minutes, but Long struck again on 68 minutes to make it 2-2.
Billericay manager Danny Scopes was pleased with what he saw from his players. "I'm delighted with the team performance," he said after the game.

body: Chelmsford City fought back from a goal down to beat Farnborough 2-1 in the National League South on Saturday. The Clarets trailed at half-time but scored twice after the break to take all three points in front of their home supporters.

Farnborough captain Max Ehmer opened the scoring on 34 minutes. Clarke levelled six minutes into the second half, finishing after a run and cross from Barham, and Barham then struck from the penalty spot on 70 minutes to put City in front.

It was an eventful afternoon for Odegah, who had an early header ruled out for offside and was later booked for simulation after going down in the box. City saw out the closing minutes to secure the win, watched by a crowd of 1,523.

stories.headline: c2c trains delayed across network after fire near Grays line
stories.summary: A fire on land beside the railway at Grays slowed c2c trains on every route. Lines have reopened, but delays may last into the evening.
body: c2c trains were cancelled and delayed on every route on the afternoon of Friday 27 November, after a fire on property next to the railway at Grays forced trains to slow down on all lines.

By 4.08pm c2c said all lines had reopened, but warned trains could still be cancelled or changed while services recover. It expects disruption until about 6pm. The operator has not said what caught fire. The line's troubles follow [an extra £2m reliability plan](/story/c2c-gbr-anglia-2m-reliability-plan-december-works/) announced on Thursday.

stories.headline: Buses replace trains across south Essex this weekend
stories.summary: Rail passengers from Shenfield, Southend and the Crouch Valley face replacement buses on Saturday and Sunday. Dartford Crossing works are paused for Black Friday.
body: Rail passengers across south Essex face a weekend of replacement buses on Saturday 28 and Sunday 29 November. Transport for London says no Elizabeth line trains will run between Paddington and Shenfield on either day. Buses run instead from Shenfield to Chadwell Heath and Newbury Park, and from Stratford to Romford.
## Greater Anglia

Network Rail is also maintaining the Southend Victoria and Southminster lines. Buses replace trains from Southend Victoria and from Ingatestone to Newbury Park, the Central line station in east London, and between Southminster and Wickford. Trains from Norwich, Ipswich and Clacton run only as far as Shenfield, where passengers change to buses via Ingatestone. Underground tickets are accepted between Newbury Park and Stratford or Liverpool Street, as [The Seax reported on Monday](/story/southend-victoria-southminster-lines-rail-buses-28-29-november/).
## Roads

In Wickford, Station Approach is shut on both days, and First Essex's 13, 13A, 13B and X10 buses take a diversion. Drivers heading for Kent get a clear run at night. National Highways says it will not close the Dartford Crossing tunnels or the QEII Bridge overnight from Friday 27 November until 3 December. The pause is to help shoppers, hauliers and delivery firms through Black Friday and Cyber Monday.
## Next week

Overnight works in the Dartford west tunnel resume at 9pm on 3 December, and the east tunnel follows from 6 December. In Chelmsford, Melbourne Avenue shuts from 8pm to 5am between 30 November and 2 December for roadworks, with First Essex's C2 and C3 diverted. Looking further ahead, Greater Anglia trains will not run between Shenfield and London Liverpool Street from 27 December to 3 January.

stories.headline: Thurrock Council says sorry over Grays Town Park cafe rent demand
stories.summary: A Reform councillor says the demand was sent without authorisation. The council will meet the volunteers to agree a way forward.
body: Thurrock Council has apologised to the volunteers who run the Grays Town Park cafe for the way they were told to start paying rent, and says it will meet them to agree a way forward.

"We are sorry that they received this email out of the blue, which we recognise will have caused them a good deal of stress and upset," the council said. Its statement was shared on Facebook on Friday afternoon by Reform UK councillor Steven Pester. The council added that it wanted to see the cafe "continue and thrive" in the park.

The council said it was reviewing all its historic arrangements with businesses, charities and community groups based in council-owned buildings, to make sure taxpayers get value for money. It pointed out that the cafe has no lease, and has paid no rent for several years while taxpayers covered its utility bills, but said it recognised the group's "huge contribution" to Grays.

Cllr Pester, who represents Little Thurrock Blackshots, went further. He wrote that a council department had sent the rent demand "without authorisation, or accuracy", against the new administration's planned policy on fair use of council buildings. He said he had asked the council to apologise and withdraw the demand, and that other letters had been stopped. Reform UK has run the council since May, when it won 45 of the 49 seats.
The council's statement did not say whether the demand has been withdrawn, or what happens next for the other community groups that have been told to expect new charges.
## How the row began

Grays Town Park Cafe opened in 2021 in a disused shelter built in 1930 in memory of the Grays brewery owner Jonathan Seabrooke. Thurrock Council backed the project with a grant and waived the rent and utility bills. The park itself was given to the people of Thurrock in 1887.

Thurrock Nub News first reported the row on Tuesday 24 November. The Friends of Grays Town Park, who run the cafe, say the council told them the new rent reflects the building's valuation and current market conditions. Once running costs are added, the bill comes to almost £1,000 a month, which the group says it cannot sustain.

Tina Holland, who founded the cafe, told BBC News the money would have to come out of what the cafe does for the town. It is home to a book club, a yarn group, a men's health group, bike rides, free summer yoga, monthly music nights and a dementia group. Prices are kept low, and the kitchen has only a toaster and a microwave.

Volunteers also pick litter and look after the park's gardens and public toilets, Ms Holland said. The Friends warn that "we will have no option but to consider closing the cafe" unless the rent is cut sharply. Their hopes of resurfacing the park's games courts and extending the cafe are now in doubt.

Money is tight at the council, which was effectively declared bankrupt in 2022 with debts that reached £1.5bn. Councillors went through its [latest savings plans on 24 November](/story/thurrock-budget-savings-scrutiny-24-november-preview/). Nub News says it has been told of several other community groups facing new charges or steep rent rises, among them a nursery for disabled children.
points: Council: cafe has no lease and has paid no rent for years
Statement does not say whether the demand is withdrawn
Other community groups also face new charges, Nub News says

stories.headline: Epping Forest District Council backs plan to prevent homelessness
stories.summary: A new five-year plan aims to stop people in the Epping Forest district losing their homes. Requests for help are up a quarter since 2022.
body: Epping Forest District Council's cabinet approved a new Homelessness and Rough Sleeping Strategy at its meeting on Thursday 26 November. It sets out how the council and its partners will prevent homelessness, tackle rough sleeping and find better homes for residents over the next five years, to 2031.

Demand has grown sharply. The council says 1,086 households came to it for help with homelessness in 2022/23, and 1,357 did so in 2025/26. That is 271 more households a year. The plan leans on three things: stepping in early, before people lose their homes, working with partners, and getting more people into suitable housing. The previous strategy was written to cover 2022 to 2027.

Councillors also approved spending on a new communications system for the council's customer services. The council said digital tools will matter more in future, but residents will still be able to get help in person and in other ways that do not need a computer.

The meeting opened with a row over transparency. Council leader Cllr Chris Whitbread responded to concerns after public questions about Qualis Commercial, the council's own company, were turned down. He said the council was committed to openness and proper scrutiny, and that its constitution is designed to avoid repeating issues already dealt with at public meetings. Cabinet also took reports on budget monitoring, risk management and an updated debt recovery policy.
points: 1,357 households asked for help in 2025/26
New customer services system approved

stories.headline: Essex patients missed almost 37,000 GP surgery appointments in September
stories.summary: It is the highest monthly figure this year. NHS Essex is asking patients to cancel appointments they cannot make.
points: About one in every 28 appointments offered went unused
Missed GP appointments cost an estimated £465,150
Cancel through the NHS App or by phoning your surgery
body: Patients missed 36,925 appointments at GP surgeries across Essex in September, the highest monthly total so far this year, according to NHS figures.

The figures come from the county's Local Medical Committees, which represent GPs, and were published by NHS Essex, the body that plans and pays for health services in the county. They count appointments booked at surgeries where the patient did not turn up and did not cancel.

Surgeries offered 1,022,806 appointments in September, so about one in every 28 went unused. Of those missed, 11,075 were with GPs and 25,430 with nurses and other practice staff, such as clinical pharmacists and physiotherapists. For another 420, the type of staff was not recorded.

That is a little below the national rate. Across England, about one GP surgery appointment in 23 (4.3%) was missed in 2025, according to NHS England. The figures are not measured in exactly the same way: Essex's count is set against appointments offered, England's against appointments recorded.
Missed video and online appointments with GPs have risen sharply. There were 788 in September, more than four times the 171 missed in January.

NHS Essex puts the cost of the missed GP appointments at £465,150 for September and about £3.5 million since January. It works this out at £42 an appointment, an estimate of the doctor time and resources involved, and says it is not a direct financial loss to surgeries.

Dr Ian Perry, a GP and primary care partner member at NHS Essex, said people were often frustrated at not being able to get an appointment. "These are appointments that could have been given to someone else," he said.
"If you no longer need your appointment or cannot make it, please cancel in good time by using the NHS app or phoning your practice. That way, we can offer it to someone else who needs it."

September was one of five months this year in which Essex surgeries offered more than a million appointments, along with January, March, June and July. More than 45% of appointments took place on the day they were booked, and about two in three were face to face.

NHS Essex is also adding appointments to cope with winter. [Surgeries are due to offer 32,000 extra appointments this winter](/story/essex-nhs-32000-extra-gp-appointments-winter-2026/), as The Seax reported on Thursday.
Appointments can be cancelled through the NHS App or by phoning your surgery. Anyone who still needs to be seen can ask the practice to rearrange.

stories.headline: Ingatestone Festive Fair brings 30 stalls to the High Street on Sunday
stories.summary: Brentwood's Christmas lights are now on. The borough's free festive events move on to Ingatestone and Shenfield.
body: Ingatestone Festive Fair runs from 12pm to 5pm on Sunday 29 November. Brentwood Borough Council says 30 traditional market stalls will sell food, gifts and handmade goods, with live music and walkabout acts along the High Street. Entry is free.

It is the next date in the Christmas programme run by Brentwood Connected, the town centre Business Improvement District (BID), with the council. Christmas Toy Trails open in Ingatestone and Shenfield on the same day, with prizes to be won across all the trails. Festive Shenfield follows on Sunday 6 December, also from 12pm to 5pm, with funfair rides, market stalls and a Santa's grotto in Hutton Road.
## How Brentwood lit up

The season began on Saturday 21 November with Lighting Up Brentwood. A Santa Parade led by Razzamataz Theatre School made its way through the High Street. Later the Mayor of Brentwood, Councillor Nicky Cuthbert, switched on the lights, helped by the young winners of her Christmas card and poem competitions.

Sarah Walmsley, manager of Brentwood Connected, said the event was "all about bringing people together". A Christmas Window Trail is open too, with windows painted by local artists at businesses away from the High Street, including Levain Bakehouse and Tulip Café. A giant Christmas arch at the Chapel Ruins, paid for by town centre businesses, stays up through the festive season.

stories.headline: Greater Anglia shuts Shenfield to London line for 8 days after Christmas
stories.summary: Essex rail passengers face buses to the Tube for a week over New Year. Trains also finish early on Christmas Eve.
body: Greater Anglia will run no trains between Shenfield and London Liverpool Street from 27 December to 3 January while essential engineering work takes place, according to the travel advice published on National Rail. Trains from Southend Victoria, Clacton-on-Sea, Ipswich and Norwich will still run as far as Shenfield.

Passengers heading into London will need a rail replacement bus from Shenfield or Ingatestone to Newbury Park. From there they can take the Central line to Stratford or Liverpool Street at no extra cost.
## Christmas Eve, Christmas Day and Boxing Day

On Christmas Eve, services start thinning out from 7pm and stop by 10pm. The Stansted Express runs later: the last train to the airport leaves Liverpool Street at 11.21pm, and the last from the airport leaves at 11.58pm.

Rob Mullen, GBR Anglia's chief customer and commercial officer, said: "Our trains will finish earlier than usual on Christmas Eve." There are no trains on Christmas Day. On Boxing Day the only service is a limited Stansted Express between the airport and Tottenham Hale, calling at Harlow Town and Bishop's Stortford. Tickets can be used on the Underground between Tottenham Hale and Liverpool Street at no extra cost.
## More work in the new year

Late on Monday 4 January, work near Clacton changes two trains. The 10.56pm from Colchester to Walton-on-the-Naze will end at Clacton-on-Sea, with a bus on to Walton via Kirby Cross and Frinton-on-Sea. The 11.18pm from Liverpool Street to Clacton will be replaced by a bus between Colchester and Clacton.

The festive closure comes before the weekend cancellations planned on lines into London early next year, [as The Seax reported](/story/essex-greater-anglia-elizabeth-line-weekend-cancellations-early-2027/). Greater Anglia is asking passengers to check before they travel, both on Christmas Eve and across the holiday.
points: Christmas Day: no Greater Anglia trains at all
Buses run from Shenfield and Ingatestone to Newbury Park

stories.headline: One in three Essex takeaways misses top food hygiene rating
stories.summary: The Seax checked every food hygiene rating in Essex. Takeaways fare worst, and Tendring's lag the rest of the county.
points: Fewer than half of Tendring's takeaways are rated 5
Seven places to eat rated 0, urgent improvement necessary
418 places to eat still await a first inspection
Castle Point has no place to eat rated below 3
body: Every restaurant, takeaway, pub and cafe in England is given a food hygiene rating from 0 to 5 by its local council. Inspectors look at how food is handled, the state of the kitchen and how well the business manages food safety. A 5 means very good. A 0 means urgent improvement is necessary.

The ratings are public, but businesses in England do not have to display them. With the Christmas party season starting, The Seax has gone through every rating held by Essex's 14 councils, covering 15,436 food businesses, as published by the Food Standards Agency on 27 November.

Most places to eat out in Essex do well. Of the 6,732 restaurants, cafes, takeaways, pubs, hotels and mobile caterers with a rating, 5,289 (79%) have the top score. Only 159 (2%) were rated 2 or below.

Takeaways are the exception. Of 1,254 rated takeaways and sandwich shops, 839 have a 5. That leaves 415, one in three, below the top rating. For restaurants, cafes and pubs the figure is about one in five.
Most of those 415 takeaways are not failing. 232 were rated 4, meaning good, and 152 were rated 3, generally satisfactory. Thirty-one were rated 2 or below.
Where you live makes a difference. In Tendring, 62 of 135 rated takeaways (46%) have a 5. It is the only Essex council area where fewer than half do. Thurrock is next lowest at 53%.
Castle Point does best: 66 of its 74 rated takeaways (89%) have a 5. Uttlesford (87%) and Maldon (82%) follow.

Tendring also has the lowest share of places to eat rated 5 overall, at 59.5%, and the most rated 2 or below, with 28. Rochford has the highest share of low ratings: 15 of its 258 rated places to eat (5.8%). Castle Point has none rated below 3.
Seven places to eat out were rated 0, urgent improvement necessary, at their most recent inspection. In Basildon, De-Source Africa Restaurant/ Miolad on Southernhay was inspected in February 2026.

In Colchester, Coffee Link at Colchester railway station was rated 0 in April 2025 and Bees Indian Restaurant & Bar in the High Street in October 2026. In Southend, Pallavas in London Road was rated 0 in September 2026.

In Clacton, Efes BBQ in Old Road was rated 0 in June 2026 and Welcome 168 Ltd in North Road in September 2026. The Bull And Willow Ltd, which runs The Bull in Great Totham, was rated 0 in September 2026 and has a new rating pending.

A rating shows what inspectors found on the day. Businesses can make improvements and ask the council to inspect again, and some may already have done so. The Food Standards Agency's website always shows the latest rating.

There is also a waiting list. 418 places to eat out in Essex are still waiting for their first inspection, usually because they have recently opened or changed hands. Colchester has the most, with 80, followed by Uttlesford with 69.
Some ratings are old, too. 184 places to eat were last inspected more than five years ago. Councils set how often they inspect each business according to the risk it poses.

How we did this: The Seax downloaded every food hygiene rating held by Essex's 14 councils from the Food Standards Agency on 27 November 2026. We checked the totals against the agency's own daily data files for each council. Places to eat out are the agency's restaurant, cafe and canteen, takeaway and sandwich shop, pub and bar, hotel and B&B, and mobile caterer categories. Businesses that are exempt, awaiting inspection or awaiting publication are left out of the percentages.
If you are worried about hygiene at a food business, you can report it to the local council through the Food Standards Agency's website.

stories.headline: Lakeside's Slim Chickens restaurant opens on 10 December
stories.summary: The US chicken chain is bringing 50 jobs to the Thurrock shopping centre. Its first 5,000 customers each get a prize card.
body: Slim Chickens will open its restaurant on Level 1 of Lakeside Shopping Centre in West Thurrock at noon on Thursday 10 December. The East Anglia Gazette reported the confirmed date, three weeks after the chain first said it was coming before Christmas.

Your Thurrock reported on 6 November that the restaurant would create 50 jobs and serve dine-in, takeaway and delivery customers. It will be the ninth Slim Chickens run by franchise partner JRK Restaurants, part of the Boparan Restaurant Group. The group already has Essex restaurants in Basildon, Chelmsford and Colchester.
## What the opening offers

The first 5,000 people to order will get a card with a code to enter in the Slim Chickens app. Prizes include free chicken tenders, sandwiches, shakes and Texas toast. One card hides a pass worth free Slim Chickens for life. The first 100 customers through the doors on opening day also get free chicken tenders.

Jitenda Thakur, general manager of the Lakeside restaurant, said the firm was proud to be creating jobs in the area. Students will be able to get 20% off their bill from Sunday to Thursday, according to Your Thurrock.

stories.headline: Maldon High Street arson: police appeal for information
stories.summary: Two people tried to break into a High Street business and start a fire at about 2.30am. Salt Bar Pizza Grill says it is open as usual.
points: Police log: incident 83 of Friday 27 November
Salt and next-door Sark are both open
body: Essex Police is investigating reports of an arson in Maldon High Street in the early hours of Friday.
Emergency services were called at about 2.30am to reports that two people had tried to force their way into a business and start a fire before leaving the area, the force said.
Officers and firefighters went to the scene to make it safe. Police said enquiries are continuing.

Salt Bar Pizza Grill says it is open as usual. Its manager, Robert Muca, said a gas meter seen in pictures of the damage has nothing to do with the restaurant. "The gas meter serves the residential flats above and is entirely unrelated to Salt Bar & Restaurant," he told Maldon Community Hub.
"We remain open and are operating as usual without any disruption."

Sark Restaurant & Cocktail Bar, next door, posted on Facebook earlier, before Salt commented. It said it had been "a difficult evening for our neighbours at SALT following an unfortunate break-in and attempted fire at their restaurant".
Sark said its staff were there to lend a hand. "As a community, it's important that we stand together and support one another, especially during difficult times," it said.
Sark said it had not been affected and was open from 11am as usual.
Police have not said whether anyone was hurt or whether any arrests have been made.

Anyone with information, including dashcam, doorbell or CCTV footage from the High Street overnight, should contact Essex Police online or on 101, quoting incident 83 of Friday 27 November. Information can also be given anonymously to Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111.

stories.headline: Essex urgent treatment centres under review
stories.summary: NHS Essex wants to hear where people go when they need help fast. Its survey will shape a new plan for urgent care.
points: More than 730,000 A&E visits in Essex each year
Survey closes at 5pm on Monday 4 January
Paper copies from essexicb.getinvolved@nhs.net
body: NHS Essex is reviewing the county's urgent treatment centres and minor injuries units, and wants to hear from patients before it decides what happens to them.

Urgent treatment centres sit between a GP and A&E. They see problems that need treating the same day but are not life-threatening, such as sprains, suspected broken bones, cuts, minor burns and eye or skin problems. Most treat adults and children aged two and over.

In Essex they include the centres at Colchester Hospital, Clacton Hospital and Princess Alexandra Hospital in Harlow, alongside a minor injuries unit at Thurrock Community Hospital in Grays, according to NHS Essex.

The health service says Essex sees more than 730,000 A&E attendances a year. Many people who turn up do not need an emergency department, and NHS Essex wants more of them seen closer to home so A&E can focus on the most seriously ill.

A new public survey asks where people would go when they need medical help quickly, what happened when they used local services and what would make care easier to reach. It is open to everyone, whether or not they have used urgent or emergency care recently.

The answers will feed into an urgent and emergency care strategy, due in the first half of 2027. It will look at options for the future of urgent treatment centres across the county. NHS Essex says any changes would need more planning, public engagement and formal approval first.

Samantha Goldberg, executive director of commercial, resilience and estates at NHS Essex, said: "We know how important it is for people to get help quickly when they are unwell or injured." She said the aim was a more consistent and joined-up approach across Essex, with emergency services kept free for those who need them most.
The review follows an earlier NHS Essex survey of 2,200 people. They said they wanted faster access to care, services closer to home and clearer information about where to go for help.

In August, NHS Essex set out plans to move Thurrock's minor injuries unit from Orsett Hospital to Thurrock Community Hospital, backed by £1m. In the longer term it wants a full urgent treatment centre there.
The survey takes about 10 minutes and is on the Essex Virtual Views website. It closes at 5pm on Monday 4 January 2027. Anyone who would prefer a paper copy can email essexicb.getinvolved@nhs.net.
If you are unwell and unsure where to go, NHS 111 can advise by phone or online at any time. In an emergency, call 999.
